Exam strategy
1.     Formula প্রথমে symbol + unit সহ শিখবে; তারপর ১টি derivation বুঝবে।
2.     Theory answer: Definition m echanism /factors t able /sketch d esign significance c onclusion .
3.     Proof/derivation: Given concept assumptions /definition algebra /energy balance final boxed relation.
4.     প্রতি Section-এ ৪ set থেকে ৩ set answer করতে হয়; তাই repeated theory + derivation/numerical mix প্রস্তুত রাখবে.

Important source caution
 No invented shading formula

 বানিয়ে দেয়নি। Instructor-verified sun-angle method থাকলে সেটাই follow করবে.

 specification • Microclimate • Shading • Climate-friendly movements • Ventilation / air-space / infiltration.

A1. Climatic Comfort Indices
Effective Temperature (ET)
 Different air-temperature + humidity combinations can feel equally comfortable.
 ET scale combines Temperature + Humidity + Air movement on a psychrometric basis.
 Radiation effect is not included in basic ET.

Corrected Effective Temperature (CET)
 ET scale is corrected by incorporating radiation effect.
 Hence CET is more complete than ET where radiant environment matters.

Equivalent Warmth (EW) & Operative Temperature (OT)
 EW correlates air temperature, humidity, mean radiant temperature with skin/clothing surface temperature.
 OT combines effects of radiation and air temperature; humidity and air movement are treated as negligible in the lecture
  slide.
 Shortcut - ET-CET
 ET = T + H + Air movement. CET = ET + Radiation.

A4. Human Heat Exchange & Heat Loss

                          Conduction, convection, radiation and evaporation are the main exchange modes .

 Conduction: direct contact surface-এর মাধ্যমে.
 Convection: skin/clothing-এর সাথে contact air; air movement বাড়লে convective exchange বাড়ে.
 Radiation: contact ছাড়া body   ↔ surrounding surface/sun.

pages.title:  Evaporation: sweat, perspiration and exhalation; dry air evaporation বাড়ায়.
pages.text:
 Evaporation: sweat, perspiration and exhalation; dry air evaporation বাড়ায়.
Repeated theory
Heat loss in different climatic situations repeatedly appears. Core logic: convection stops when air temperature
approaches skin temperature; radiation depends on surrounding surface temperature; hot/humid conditions make
evaporation + air movement critical.

pages.text:
Derivation idea: প্রতি ঘণ্টায় replaced air volume = nV. Mass/hour = ρnV. Heat/hour = mass × cp × ΔT. প্রতি second-এ rate
পেতে 3600 দিয়ে ভাগ।
 Source note
 Repeated QB numerical gives room volume, air changes/hour, ΔT and specific heat. The uploaded slide does not print the
 final heat-loss equation; the above is an explicitly marked reconstruction from the heat-energy relation used to solve that
 question.

A7. Microclimate & Building Envelope

                Roof, wall, floor, opening and other envelope components respond differently to heat, humidity, wind and rain .

  Roof: heat enters mainly by conduction after solar heating; time lag and heat conserving capacity matter.
  External walls: orientation changes solar exposure; east/west walls receive strong low-angle sun.
  Window/opening: admits solar heat, daylight, rain/fog and also acts as infiltration path.
  Ventilator/clerestory: higher-level hot-air exhaust can improve ventilation.
  Design tools: material, orientation, opening, architectural design, micro-planning, semi-mechanized techniques.

 Types: horizontal, vertical, combined.

pages.title: A9. Climate-friendly Movements
pages.text:
A9. Climate-friendly Movements
Tube House

                     Tube-house section concept: section form and adjustable openings support natural air movement .

 Prototype housing idea; section/profile encourages natural ventilation.
 Openings can be adjusted for different seasons/time of day.
 Courtyard/patio and high-low airflow paths can support passive comfort.

Rat-trap Bond

                                          Brick-on-edge construction creates an internal cavity.

 Bricks placed vertically/on edge create a cavity while wall width remains about 230 mm.
 Lecture notes cite reduced material use and improved thermal/sound insulation.
 Solid courses are required at top/bottom, sill/lintel and around openings.

Green vs Sustainable Building
 Green building focuses on measurable environmental performance: less water, energy efficiency, resource conservation,
  less waste, healthier spaces.
 Sustainable building additionally balances environmental, social and economic dimensions.

B1. Solar Radiation & Earth-Sun Relation
 Solar radiation is the dominant climatic energy source.
 Slide spectrum: about 290-2300 nm; UV 290-380 nm, visible 380-700 nm, short IR 700-2300 nm.
 Solar constant in lecture: 1395 W/m² at top of atmosphere.
 Earth axis is 66.5° to orbital plane; direct-sun point migrates between Tropic of Cancer and Capricorn, producing seasons.
 Equinox around 21 March and 23 September: solar radiation normal to equator.

                                   Earth-axis tilt explains seasonal migration of direct solar radiation .

Ground receives 23% + 27% = 50%. Ground sends back 20% + 20% + 10% = 50%. তাই দীর্ঘমেয়াদে ground heat budget

pages.title: B4. Global Wind Pattern, Thermal Force, Coriolis & ITCZ
pages.text:
B4. Global Wind Pattern, Thermal Force, Coriolis & ITCZ

                                          Global pressure/wind belts and circulation cells.

 Equator gets intense heating w
                               arm air rises equatorial low pressure.
 Subtropical region: cooled upper air sinks high pressure.
 Thermal force drives convection from pressure/temperature differences.
 Earth rotation modifies motion; Coriolis deflects winds. Trade winds are the resultant of thermal and Coriolis effects.
 At equator, N and S trade winds converge: Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ), often calm/light irregular breeze =
  doldrums.

                                    ITCZ follows maximum solar heating north-south seasonally .

Shortcut - 0-30-60-90
0° Low, 30° High, 60° Low, 90° High - pressure belts মনে রাখার দ্রুত sequence.

B9. Thermal Comfort & Human Heat Balance
 Metabolism converts food into living matter and energy; basal and muscular metabolism are two divisions .
 Lecture slide: about 20% of produced heat is used internally; remaining 80% is surplus and must be dissipated.
 Heat gain modes: metabolism, conduction from warm contact object, convection from warm air, radiation from hot
  objects/sun.
 Heat loss: convection, radiation, evaporation and lesser conduction.
 Deep-body temperature stays around 37°C; steady state requires surplus heat to be dissipated.

pages.title: PART IV — PROOF / DERIVATION BANK
pages.text:
PART IV — PROOF / DERIVATION BANK
 How to write derivation in exam
 প্রথম line-এ law/definition লিখবে, প্রতিটি symbol define করবে, diagram থাকলে draw করবে, algebra 3-5 steps-এ
 রাখবে, শেষে boxed final relation + physical meaning লিখবে।

D1. Cosine Law — derivation

5.   ধরা যাক parallel solar beam-এর normal intensity = In এবং surface normal-এর সাথে incidence angle = β.
6.   একই beam bundle normal surface-এ projected area B এবং tilted surface-এ larger actual area C-তে ছড়িয়ে পড়ে.
7.   Geometry থেকে cos β = B/C, অর্থাৎ B = C cos β.
8.   একই total radiation energy হলে intensity ∝ 1/area. তাই tilted surface-এর intensity = In × (B/C).
9.   B/C = cos β বসালে Iβ = In cos β.

                                                        Iβ = In cos β
                                    β = 0° ⇒ maximum intensity; β increases ⇒ intensity falls.
                                                                                                      Directly stated in uploaded source

D2. Relative Humidity relation — definition proof
10. AH = given temperature-এ air-এ actual moisture content.
11. SH = same temperature-এ maximum/saturation moisture capacity.
12. Relative humidity মানে actual capacity-এর fraction, expressed as percentage.
13. Fraction = AH/SH. Percentage করতে ×100.

                                             RH = (AH / SH) × 100 %
                           All humidity quantities must be expressed on the same mass/volume basis.
                                                                                                      Directly stated in uploaded source

D3. Earth’s Thermal Balance — accounting proof
14. Incoming solar energy = 100% ধরা হয়.
15. 5% ground reflection + 20% cloud reflection + 25% atmosphere absorption = 50% diverted before/around ground
     heating.
16. Ground receives diffuse 23% + direct 27% = 50%.
17. Ground loses 20% long-wave + 20% evaporation then radiation + 10% convection then radiation = 50%.
18. Therefore ground input = ground output = 50%; long-term thermal balance is maintained in the lecture model .

     Ground gain = 23% + 27% = 50% = 20% + 20% + 10% = Ground loss

pages.title: Course-slide percentage accounting.
pages.text:
Course-slide percentage accounting.
                                                                                                                Directly stated in uploaded source

D4. Human Heat Balance — energy-conservation derivation
19. Metabolism (Met) produces internal body heat.
20. Evaporation (Evp) always removes latent heat, so it is written as a loss term.
21. Conduction (Cnd), convection (Cnv) and radiation (Rad) may be gain or loss depending on environmental temperature
    gradients; hence ± signs.
22. Steady deep-body temperature means net heat storage = 0.
23. Therefore all gains and losses algebraically sum to zero.

                                    Met − Evp ± Cnd ± Cnv ± Rad = 0
  If the sum departs from zero, vasomotor adjustment occurs; persistent overheating leads to sweating, underheating to shivering.
                                                                                                                Directly stated in uploaded source

D5. Air Changes per Hour (ACH) — derivation
24. Q = ventilation flow rate in m³/s.
25. One hour = 3600 s, তাই one hour-এ supplied/replaced air volume = 3600Q m³.
26. Room volume = V m³.
27. Number of complete room-volume replacements per hour = supplied volume per hour / room volume.
28. Hence ACH = 3600Q / V.

                                                     ACH = 3600 Q / V
                                                            Q in m³/s, V in m³.
                                                                                                       Derived for solving repeated QB numericals

D6. Total Fresh-air Requirement — derivation
29. If each person needs qperson L/s, N persons need N identical shares.
30. Total required supply = sum of individual supplies = N × qperson.
31. Convert L/s to m³/s by dividing by 1000.

                         Qtotal = N qperson ;                        Q(m³/s) = Q(L/s) / 1000
                                          Use the lecture fresh-air table to choose qperson.
                                                                                                       Derived for solving repeated QB numericals

D7. Heat Loss due to Air Change — derivation
32. Room volume V, air changes n per hour ⇒ air volume replaced per hour = nV.
33. If air density = ρ, mass replaced per hour = ρnV.
34. For temperature difference ΔT, heat carried per hour = mass × cp × ΔT = ρnVcpΔT.
35. Heat-loss rate per second = divide by 3600.
36. Thus Q̇ air = ρVncpΔT / 3600.

                                             Q̇ air = ρ V n cp ΔT / 3600
         Standard reconstruction for the repeated air-change heat-loss numerical; not printed verbatim in uploaded slide.
                                                                                                       Derived for solving repeated QB numericals

D8. Driving Rain Index — relation, not a mathematical proof
                                                         DRI = R × Vw
                                 R = annual rainfall (m), Vw = annual average wind speed (m/s).
                                                                                                                Directly stated in uploaded source
